:::{#exm-shape-rule}
#### Shape of a product of three matrices

<!-- no-figure: the example works with shapes only, so there are no values to plot -->

Let $\matr{A}$ be $2 \times 3$,
let $\matr{B}$ be $3 \times 4$,
and let $\vx \in \reals^4$,
which is a $4 \times 1$ [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix).
Apply the [shape rule](#def-shape-rule) one [product](#def-matrix-mult) at a time:

- $\matr{A}\matr{B}$ is $(2 \times 3)(3 \times 4)$.
  The inner pair $3, 3$ matches,
  so the product is $2 \times 4$.
- $(\matr{A}\matr{B})\vx$ is $(2 \times 4)(4 \times 1)$.
  The inner pair $4, 4$ matches,
  so the product is $2 \times 1$,
  a vector in $\reals^2$.

:::
